title: A pocket calculator
description:
Write a calculator for one sum. It asks for a number, an operation and a second number, then prints the result:

```
First number? 7
Operation (+ - * / // % ^)? /
Second number? 2
7 / 2 = 3.5
```

- The operations are `+ - * / // % ^`. Read the operation as a whole line.
- Print the result as Lua prints it: `7 // 2 = 3`, `2 ^ 10 = 1024.0`, `1.5 + 1 = 2.5`.
- If either number is not a number, print `That is not a number.` and nothing else.
- If the operation is not one of the seven, print `Unknown operation: <what was typed>`.
- `/`, `//` and `%` by zero print `Cannot divide by zero.`
- After the result, print a second line describing it: `The result is a whole number.` when it is a whole number (also `1024.0`), otherwise `The result has decimals.`

Ask all three questions before printing any message, even when the first answer is already wrong.

starter.main.lua:
io.write("First number? ")
local a = tonumber(io.read())
io.write("Operation (+ - * / // % ^)? ")
local op = io.read()
io.write("Second number? ")
local b = tonumber(io.read())
print(a + b)

solution.main.lua:
io.write("First number? ")
local a = tonumber(io.read())
io.write("Operation (+ - * / // % ^)? ")
local op = io.read()
io.write("Second number? ")
local b = tonumber(io.read())

if not a or not b then
    print("That is not a number.")
elseif op ~= "+" and op ~= "-" and op ~= "*" and op ~= "/" and op ~= "//" and op ~= "%" and op ~= "^" then
    print("Unknown operation: " .. op)
elseif (op == "/" or op == "//" or op == "%") and b == 0 then
    print("Cannot divide by zero.")
else
    local result
    if op == "+" then result = a + b
    elseif op == "-" then result = a - b
    elseif op == "*" then result = a * b
    elseif op == "/" then result = a / b
    elseif op == "//" then result = a // b
    elseif op == "%" then result = a % b
    else result = a ^ b
    end
    print(tostring(a) .. " " .. op .. " " .. tostring(b) .. " = " .. tostring(result))
    if result == math.floor(result) then
        print("The result is a whole number.")
    else
        print("The result has decimals.")
    end
end

hints: Check the problems first, in the order the task lists them, and only then work out the result in an `if ... elseif` chain.
A number is whole when `n == math.floor(n)`. That is true for `1024.0` too.
requirements: Every operation gives the right result.
Bad numbers, unknown operations and division by zero give their messages.
The second line says whether the result is whole.
stretch: - Accept the whole sum on one line, like `7 / 2`, once you have read lesson 4.02 on patterns.
